name: Friedrich Merz
summary: Merz is a market-oriented Christian Democrat who leads a CDU-CSU/SPD government. He stresses competitiveness, deregulation, a conditional welfare system, strict limits on irregular migration, a much larger Bundeswehr and firm NATO and EU ties, while accepting some state action such as a social state and a security-driven change to the debt brake.

sources.usedFor: His shift on same-sex couples: 2000 opposition to the civil-partnership law, 2018 support for Ehe für alle

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Described as an economic liberal from the CDU's pro-business wing; his 2008 book 'Mehr Kapitalismus wagen' argues for more market economy, and the 2025 programme he led makes market-based energy, climate and business policy its default. Davos 2026: Germany and Europe 'wasted incredible potential for growth ... by unnecessarily and excessively curtailing entrepreneurial freedoms and personal responsibility'.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Mixed: the programme he led rejects a wealth tax, but in July 2026 he announced that the highest incomes would be 'somewhat' more burdened in the income-tax reform as a contribution to social justice. Not 'significantly higher'.

unions-good.rationale: The 2025 programme he led aims for higher collective-bargaining coverage and calls social partnership the key to good wages; the coalition agreement he signed adds a federal Tariftreue law for public contracts.

regulate-corporations.rationale: His programme and government pursue deregulation of business: abolishing the German supply-chain law, ending gold-plating of EU rules and cutting reporting duties (July 2026: all reporting obligations to lapse unless re-justified). Davos 2026 (his own words, so raised to high): 'we have become the world champion of overregulation. That has to end'; 'We must reduce bureaucracy substantially in Europe'; Germany and Europe were 'excessively curtailing entrepreneurial freedoms'.

cut-welfare.rationale: Replaced the Bürgergeld with a stricter Grundsicherung (in force 1 July 2026) that demands self-responsibility and return performance; he frames reform of the welfare state as a priority. Not a general cut of all welfare programmes.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Programme he led: mandatory IP-address retention, more video cameras and automated face recognition at hotspots, stronger intelligence services (also in his 2026 Munich speech).

legalize-drugs.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: At Munich in 2026 he said freedom of speech ends where speech turns against human dignity and the Basic Law; programme he led tightens the incitement-to-hatred offence and prosecutes antisemitic and anti-constitutional statements.

state-harmful.rationale: In his 2026 Munich speech he said not only too much state power but also too little state power destroys the foundation of freedom, and that Germany accepts responsibility for acting with power.

limit-guns.rationale: Programme he led wants gun law applied strictly to extremists and criminals but says legal owners, hunters, collectors and sport shooters must not be harassed or criminalised.

empower-police-military.rationale: Programme he led strengthens police and prosecutors with more powers; he pledged in his first government statement to give the Bundeswehr all funds needed to become Europe's strongest conventional army.

decide-locally.rationale: Programme he led: 'full subsidiarity', a federalism with strong Länder and municipalities, 'who orders pays', and more weight for local practice in lawmaking.

rehabilitation.rationale: Programme he led: tougher criminal law, faster trials, 'the punishment must follow the deed at once', zero tolerance, ankle monitors; no emphasis on rehabilitation.

traditional-family.rationale: Programme he led: families are 'real performers' who give stability, keeps Ehegattensplitting for married couples and strengthens child-related benefits. Programme does not state a general thesis about the traditional family as foundation of society.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Reported (Sonntagsblatt 2025, citing Der Spiegel): in 2018 he backed the Ehe für alle and only objected that it was introduced too hastily ('überstürzt'), a change from his 2000 view that the civil-partnership law was unconstitutional. He has not reopened the issue since.

abortion-legal.rationale: In the 1990s he voted against liberalising abortion law; the programme he led says 'Paragraph 218 stays' as a hard-won social compromise. The current law lets early abortions go unpunished after counselling, so the evidence is mixed in effect.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Programme he led: 'We stand by our Leitkultur', cultural traditions are part of it, and the chapter 'a Germany we can be proud of again'.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Programme he led: 'the influx is too much'; in May 2025 he said 'more limitation, more rejections, more steering, more returns' and that too much uncontrolled immigration was allowed in ten years. He also recruits skilled workers and calls Germany an immigration country.

free-trade.rationale: At Munich in 2026: 'we do not believe in tariffs and protectionism, but in free trade'; he welcomed provisional application of EU-Mercosur and the finished EU-India deal. Davos 2026: favours countries that 'see greater benefit in free trade than in protectionism and isolationism'; 'Europe's trade ambitions are crystal clear. We want to be the alliance offering open markets and trade opportunities.'

nation-first.rationale: Programme he led says to represent legitimate national interests strategically; but in Munich he said 'never again will we Germans go alone' and framed Germany's goals European and with partners.

open-borders.rationale: Programme he led and his government: permanent border controls, rejection of irregular entries at the border, asylum seekers to be processed in safe third countries; on day one he ordered stricter border control.

limit-growth.rationale: In his first government statement he vowed to do everything to put Germany back on a growth path and to make competitiveness the yardstick of economic policy. Davos 2026: 'we want to ensure that our economy can tap into its full potential for innovation and growth'; Mercosur has 'no alternative ... if we want to have higher growth in Europe'.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Government keeps the German, EU and international climate targets but wants 'new paths'; programme: market-based climate policy, abolish the heating law, ends the combustion engine ban; in 2023 he called climate overrated in the debate.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Mixed: called the exit a 'serious strategic mistake' (Jan 2026) and backs research on SMRs and fusion, but as chancellor ruled out a return to nuclear power, calling the exit irreversible.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The programme he led raises inheritance-tax allowances (including for family homes) and rejects a wealth tax; no call for heavier inheritance taxation.

basic-income.rationale: Government replaced the Bürgergeld with a conditional Grundsicherung based on reciprocity; the programme says 'Fördern und Fordern muss immer gelten'. Direct opposite of an unconditional income, though he did not comment on basic income by name.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Munich 2026: 'we do not believe in tariffs and protectionism'; in 2025 he sought a trade deal with the lowest possible tariffs because it serves the export economy. Davos 2026: 'Tariffs again have to be replaced by rules' and Europe 'must be the antithesis to ... arbitrary tariffs'.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Davos 2026: the state is 'investing in high-performance AI, gigafactories, speeding up the expansion of data centres', '€500 billion have been made available' for infrastructure and there is 'more targeted support to innovators'; but he frames the aim as 'to mobilize private sector investments ... with clear rules', so agree, not strongly.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Programme chapter on more property, wealth formation and old-age provision (higher allowances for home purchase, savings; Frühstart-Rente for 6-18 year olds). Does not address concentration in corporations or the state directly.

democracy-best.rationale: Frames Germany's foreign policy around democracies, saying 'autocracies have followers; democracies have partners', and in 2026 rejects banning the AfD as a substitute for winning voters back.

military-superiority.rationale: Wants the strongest conventional army in Europe and credible deterrence of Russia; this is about deterrence and not explicit superiority over every rival.

conscription.rationale: Programme he led introduces a 'growing' Wehrpflicht as necessary for peace and security; his government's law (Dec 2025) brings mandatory screening for men and lets the Bundestag order compulsory service if volunteers fall short.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Programme he led: Israel's right to exist is German Staatsräson, with friendship 'unshakeable'; he has repeatedly said Germany stands on Israel's side, while criticising Gaza operations as disproportionate in 2025.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Mixed: the programme he led promised to keep the debt brake and said debts are tomorrow's tax rises, and in May 2025 he urged caution with new debt; but in March 2025 he agreed a Basic Law change exempting defence above 1% of GDP and a 500 bn euro infrastructure fund.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Government suspended family reunification for subsidiary-protection holders and applies 'bed, bread and soap' benefits for those obliged to leave; he has said certain welfare payments should not go to non-working or arriving migrants. Not a general reservation for citizens.

work-for-welfare.rationale: In his July 2026 government statement he named the new Grundsicherung, 'with which we demand self-responsibility and something in return again from those who can'; programme: 'Fördern und Fordern muss immer gelten'.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Programme he led demands a clear commitment to freedom, equality, democracy and rule of law and a Leitkultur, and 'integration demanded more intensively'; it does not ask immigrants to give up their original culture.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He leads a government that expands the state well beyond defence and justice: a 'strong and fair welfare state', pensions, housing, research and industrial policy are in the programme and coalition agreement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Programme he led: human rights are 'universal, indivisible and inalienable'; in Munich he tied freedom to human dignity under the Basic Law.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Mixed: he does not reject the instrument (said in Sept 2026 that a ban can be examined repeatedly and he would not close himself to banning the 'völkisch' wing), but he says he is and remains sceptical, calls the hurdle very high, and prefers political confrontation with the AfD.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: His government abolished the traffic-light fast-track naturalisation (3 years); programme: 'the German passport comes at the end of integration, not at the start'.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Munich 2026: 'Europe's unification and strengthening is our most noble task' and 'if Europe breaks apart, Germany breaks apart'; he supports an EU security pillar. He also insists on subsidiarity and refuses liability for other states' debts.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Munich 2026: Germany 'remains true' to NATO and builds a stronger European pillar inside the alliance, not instead of it. Davos 2026: 'we should not give up on NATO' and 'we must repair the trust on which the alliance is built'.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Mixed: programme says 'our Christian view of humanity commands us to help the poorest' and humanitarian aid, but ties development policy to migration, security and geopolitical aims and merges aid ministries for efficiency.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: In Munich 2026 he said he had started talks with France on European nuclear deterrence, strictly within Germany's legal obligations and NATO nuclear sharing; no German national arsenal sought.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Programme he led states commitment to the independence of the ECB, expects it to protect price stability and fight inflation, and rejects state financing by the ECB.

collective-defense.rationale: Munich 2026: reminded that Article 42 TEU commits EU states to assist each other and NATO rests on trust; programme: 'NATO is our security guarantee'. Davos 2026, on Greenland: 'We will protect Denmark, Greenland, the North from the threat posed by Russia', within NATO.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Davos 2026: 'There is no room for isolationism and protectionism in this agenda. Instead, we are talking about strategically coordinated ties worldwide', and he praises countries that 'see greater benefit in free trade than in protectionism and isolationism'.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Programme he led: 'we are for keeping animals', with funding for welfare-friendly stalls and mandatory labelling of welfare and origin, and against cuts or quotas.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Davos 2026, on US pressure over Greenland: 'Democracies do not have subordinates. They have allies, partners and trusted friends', and (in German) 'This world, we are not subordinate to it.' Rests on these short passages, so medium.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The 2025 programme he led would repeal the Selbstbestimmungsgesetz (self-determination law); the coalition agreement he signed only provides for an evaluation, so the law stayed in force.

assisted-dying.rationale: Programme he led rejects 'active' euthanasia (aktive Sterbehilfe) and instead expands hospice and palliative care and a suicide-prevention law; it does not address legal assisted suicide as such.

social-market-economy.rationale: The coalition agreement he signed calls the social market economy a cornerstone; in May 2025 he renewed the 'promise of prosperity for all'; the programme pairs competition with an 'strong and fair welfare state'.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Pledged in May 2025 to make the Bundeswehr 'conventionally the strongest army in Europe' and set a 3.5% of GDP core defence goal. Davos 2026: 'we decided right at the start of my tenure to increase Germany's defence spending up to 5% of GDP'.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Rejects neutrality: NATO is Germany's security guarantee and Europe must stand with the US and its neighbours, as stated in Munich 2026 and the 2025 programme.

rent-control.rationale: His government extended the Mietpreisbremse (rent brake) in tight housing markets for four years, which he cited in his 2025 general debate speech; the programme also backs 'effective and appropriate tenant protection' including rent-level rules.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Munich 2026: European deterrence must be 'embedded in our nuclear sharing within NATO', which keeps US nuclear weapons in Germany.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: In December 2025 he said he expected US long-range weapons to be stationed in Germany as planned and saw no step toward dissolving the mutual security pledge; programme wants to deepen the US partnership.

online-anonymity.rationale: At the CDU's Ash Wednesday rally in Trier (Feb 2026) he said: 'I want to see real names on the internet. I want to know who is speaking up.'

pollution-taxes.rationale: Programme he led says emissions trading is the right instrument to cap emissions efficiently; in early 2026 he briefly floated abolishing the EU ETS before reaffirming climate targets.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Programme: aim of higher collective-bargaining coverage, strengthening generally binding collective agreements, wage setting is a matter for social partners; coalition agreement adds the Tariftreue law.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Mixed: programme keeps the constitutional debt brake and demands binding Maastricht criteria, but his government loosened the national rule for defence and a special infrastructure fund in 2025.

public-service-media.rationale: Coalition agreement he signed: commitment to a plural public-service broadcasting system alongside fair conditions for private media.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Programme he led: 'Without the German language integration fails', mandatory integration agreements, language tests before school age, and good German as a condition of naturalisation.

equal-conscription.rationale: Mixed: the Wehrdienst law he enacted makes the questionnaire compulsory for men only, while programme he led aims for a compulsory Gesellschaftsjahr in the long run.

close-ties-china.rationale: Programme he led: counter China's influence where strategic interests are touched, with an independent European China policy coordinated with the US; Munich 2026 says China exploits dependencies systematically.

notes: Recent positions win over older ones: as opposition leader he promised to keep the debt brake and to restart nuclear plants, but as chancellor he changed the debt brake for defence and infrastructure and ruled out a nuclear return. Party programmes and the coalition agreement are shared texts; answers resting only on them are at most medium. Many statements are null because no direct position was found. 2026-10-31 pass (Opus): read his Davos 2026 special address in full (local WEF corpus) and answered three statements it settles; the Wikipedia-only same-sex-marriage answer re-sourced to a newspaper report.
